summary.text: Mark Messmer is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 8th Congressional District. A mechanical engineer and small business owner from Jasper, he served in the Indiana House and Senate, including as Senate majority leader, before winning the open seat in 2024. His campaign materials cite endorsements from President Donald Trump and Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America.

paragraphs.text: Born September 21, 1962, in Jasper, Indiana, and raised in Southern Indiana.
Earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Purdue University (1985).
Worked as a project engineer with John Brown Engineering and Dow Chemical, and is co-owner of Messmer Mechanical; his House biography says he and his wife, Kim, are small business owners.

Served on the Holy Family School Board in Jasper from 2001 to 2004, including as president in 2003-2004, and has been a parish council member and music minister at Holy Family Catholic Church, according to his House biography.

Served in the Indiana House of Representatives (District 63) from 2008 to 2014, then in the Indiana Senate (District 48) from 2014 until he resigned in September 2024 to focus on his congressional campaign.
In the Indiana Senate, served as majority leader from 2018 to 2022 and chaired the Senate Environmental Affairs Committee and the Joint Rules Committee.
Won the May 2024 Republican primary for the open 8th District seat (38.5% to former U.S. Rep. John Hostettler's 19.7%) and the November general election, succeeding retiring Rep. Larry Bucshon.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry), the Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Strategic Forces), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Has introduced the Heat Workforce Standards Act, which would repeal a Biden-administration OSHA workplace heat-safety rule, according to Lakeshore Public Media.
Received the presidential endorsement of Donald Trump in 2026.

sources.title: Four Democrats compete for the chance to challenge Rep. Mark Messmer in Indiana's 8th Congressional District
